title: Introduce grandfathered credit allocator and soft revocation protocol for reservation changes
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Tenants with long-standing reserved capacity (committed/contractual reservations) were experiencing abrupt loss of soft-burst credit when admins changed reservation sizes or during autoscaler-driven decommit flows. This caused sudden tail-latency spikes and unhappy downstream SLAs. The goal of this PR is to introduce a backwards-compatible, opt-in "Grandfathered Credit Allocator" that preserves a decaying bucket of credit for legacy reservations and a 'soft revocation' protocol that gracefully drains these credits before hard revocation.

Design summary: The allocator maintains a per-tenant grandfathered_balance which is seeded from the reservation delta when a reservation is reduced or rebalanced. The balance decays on a configurable half-life window (default: 14d) and is eligible for consumption only when primary reservation tokens are exhausted. A soft_revocation handshake (controller -> fleet agent) allows the controller to request a staged revoke; the agent attempts to shed load within a configured grace_period (default: 10m) while emitting progress telemetry. If the tenant cannot shed by the end of grace_period, the controller performs a final hard revocation.

Key properties: (1) Smooth capacity transitions: avoids cliff-like revocations that cause transient QoS failures, (2) Observability: emits new metrics for credit levels, decay_rate, and active_revocations, (3) Autoscaler integration: the allocator signals 'effective_commitment' to autoscaler so scale decisions respect remaining grandfathered credit, (4) Safety: soft revocation is conservative by default and requires explicit opt-in via tenant config or a cluster-wide feature flag.

What this PR includes: implementation of the Grandfathered Credit Allocator, the soft revocation protocol handshake, autoscaler hooks to read effective_commitment, telemetry/metrics registration, unit + integration tests, ops docs and a small migration script to backfill existing reservation deltas for tenants that opt into the new policy.

Commits (high-level): - Add design doc for grandfathering and protocol (docs/ops/grandfathering.md) - Implement allocator core and REST/GRPC endpoints (services/fleet/allocator.go) - Integrate soft revocation handshake in reconciler (controller/autoscaler.go) - Metrics: register grandfathered_credit_* gauges and revocation_histogram (observability/metrics_registry.go) - Add unit and integration tests for decay and graceful revoke (services/fleet/allocator_test.go) - Add Helm config toggles and default parameters (charts/redwood-helm/templates/configmap.yaml)

Files changed (high level): services/fleet/allocator.go (core logic), services/fleet/allocator_test.go (tests and synthetic load harness), controller/autoscaler.go (autoscaler reads effective_commitment), observability/metrics_registry.go (new metrics and tags), docs/ops/grandfathering.md (design + ops runbook), charts/redwood-helm/templates/configmap.yaml (feature flag and tunables), scripts/migrations/backfill_grandfathered.py (migration helper).

Testing and results: - Unit tests cover decay math and edgecases for zero-length windows and negative deltas. - Integration tests simulate reservation shrink events and assert that soft revocation reduces burst-sourced requests over the configured grace_period. - Local load tests (10k QPS synthetic tenants) show reduced 99p latency spikes during reservation changes: median 99p drop from 420ms -> 140ms under a staged revoke with grandfathering enabled.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind a feature flag (disabled by default), 2) Canary enable for internal test tenants, 3) Ramp to customers that opt-in via tenant config within 2 weeks, 4) Monitor metrics for unexpected revocations and adjust decay window. Ops doc includes rollback steps and a script to remove grandfathered balances if needed.

Backward compatibility and safety: Feature is opt-in; default behavior unchanged. There is a config knob to set decay window and grace periods cluster-wide. All new metrics have sane cardinality (per-tenant tag only when balance > 0).

Related work and tickets: ENG-5618 (design), ENG-5640 (autoscaler hook), SUP-9082 (customer impact case motivating soft revocation).

review_comments: Ethan Caldwell: Please avoid exposing per-request locking on the allocator; the test harness showed a contention point at high QPS. Consider sharding by tenant hash and use lock-free atomic updates where possible.
Maya Patel: Addressed in f2b3c4d — switched to a sharded ring buffer + atomic updates and added contention test. PTAL.
Leah Kim: Can you add an explicit metric for soft_revocation_progress (0..1) so SREs can alert on stalled revocations?
Maya Patel: Added histogram and gauge soft_revocation_progress in observability registry; added to the canary dashboard screenshots in the ops doc.
Diego Ramos: Unit test failed in CI due to clock skew in decay math; please use clock control in tests.
Maya Patel: Fixed tests to inject deterministic clock source; reran CI.
Ethan Caldwell: LGTM after the fixes. Approved for merge.
CI Bot: Lint failed on first run (goimports). Second run passed after formatting commit.
Release Manager: Merged via squash commit to main.
ci_summary: Initial run: lint failed (goimports). Second run: all checks passed (unit/integration/load). Canary smoke: pass.
release_notes: Added an opt-in Grandfathered Credit Allocator to smooth reservation reductions and introduce a soft revocation protocol. New metrics: grandfathered_credit_balance, grandfathered_credit_decay_seconds, soft_revocation_progress, soft_revocation_duration_seconds. Config knobs exposed via Helm: grandfathering.enabled, grandfathering.decay_half_life, grandfathering.grace_period. Opt-in only; no default behavioral change.
changelog_entry: 2026-02-25: Introduced opt-in grandfathered credit allocator and soft revocation protocol (feature flagged). See docs/ops/grandfathering.md for runbook.
notes_for_qa: QA should run the included integration harness in services/fleet/allocator_test.go and validate soft_revocation_progress metric increments over a 10m simulated grace period. Use scripts/migrations/backfill_grandfathered.py to create a seeded balance for a test tenant.
security_impact: none (opt-in, no new permissions). The soft revocation handshake uses existing controller-agent authenticated channels.
